which_results_affected: None. The Voronoi pivotal-amplitude paper never cites "Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4", directly or through its companion paper, so the failure of Sec. 7.3 / Thm hol:disk / Thm intro:main / the FK Cardy theorem does not reach Theorem thm:main or any other result in it.
evidence: The premise that this paper cites the FK paper does not hold. (1) Bibliography (build/references.tex): its 17 entries are BL, CN, Cardy (1992 physics paper), CardyCS, DGLZ, GPS, KM, LP, LSW, V, Schramm, SS, Smirnov, SW, Tassion, Vanneuville, Zhan. The only OpenAI preprint is \bibitem{V}: "OpenAI, From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation ... 2026", which is a different paper. (2) I searched all .tex sources and the PDF text for FK, Fortuin, random-cluster, square-lattice, nested, Potts, q<4, holomorph, observable, parafermion. None of them refers to the FK paper. The only hits are unrelated: GPS's title "Pivotal, cluster, and interface measures", the paper's own Voronoi "interface strand, or wall" (01-inputs.tex:147), "four-interface transmission" (Secs 2-3), "Closed interface loops carry no information" (05-transfer.tex:60), and a generic "holomorphic function continuous on a boundary arc" (02-annuli.tex:207). (3) Cardy's formula is assumed, not imported. 00-introduction.tex:17-20: "\begin{assumption}[Scalar Cardy limit] For every bounded Jordan quadrilateral Q ... the critical crossing probability converges ... to Cardy's conformally invariant value." The main theorem is "Under Assumption~\ref{ass:cardy}, there exists a constant c_V ... lim eps^{3/4} E N_eps = c_V", and the paper says "The theorem is conditional on Assumption~\ref{ass:cardy}; it does not prove Cardy's formula for the Voronoi model." The proven Cardy results it cites are Smirnov [Smirnov] and Schramm-Smirnov [SS] for triangular-lattice site percolation, not the FK result. (4) Indirect route: I grepped the companion preprint V's sources for square-lattice / nested loops / FK interfaces. There is no citation; the only hit is a summation index "1\leq i\leq k" in 05-expansion.tex:121. So the dependency chain does not pass through V either. The paper's validity rests on Assumption ass:cardy and on V, both independent of the FK gap.
